To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical factor in inducing analogical reasoning in neural networks is not an elaborate architectural design, but rather, a training method based on the presentation of abstract relational structure in the data.
analogical reasoning can emerge in neural networks when they are trained to contrast abstract relational structures in input domains.

(1) the most effective method for inducing a capacity for analogy making in a neural network is to train it by contrasting the relational structure of its input domains, (2) this method is effective for both visual and symbolic analogy tasks, and (3) this method works even for very simple neural network architectures, including a single hidden layer with 100 neurons.

we show that the ability of neural networks to learn analogical reasoning can arise from simple architectures when trained in a particular way, but that the capacity for analogical thinking is fragile, and that the most important factor for inducing this capacity is the manner in which the data is presented.

the ability to learn analogies is not a special capacity that must be hardwired into a network.
